simple: Your computer is probably much stronger than the phones most Roblox players use. Studio can pretend to be a phone, but it cannot copy real memory limits, heat, or touch controls. This page explains why you should test your game on real devices and what to check. Testing on a cheap phone is the best way to find problems before your players do.
analogy: It is like testing a paper airplane. Throwing it inside your quiet room is not the same as throwing it outside on a windy day, where real players will be.
keyPoints: Studio runs the client and server together on a powerful computer, so it hides problems that show up on phones.
The device emulator is good for screen shapes and controls, but not for memory.
Most players use lower-end mobile devices. About 65 percent are on Android, and about 60 percent of those have only 2 to 4 GB of RAM.
Pick at least one low-end baseline device that matches your players and test on it often.
The MicroProfiler (Ctrl+Alt+F6) and Developer Console (F9) work on real devices too, and Performance Stats shows FPS, memory, and ping.
Play 10 to 15 minutes on a phone to check for thermal throttling. A slow drop in frame rate usually means the device is overheating.
Check network behavior over mobile data, not just home Wi-Fi.
Also check the feel: button size on small screens, readable text, switching between touch and controller, load times, and sound on phone speakers.

terms.emulation: Pretending to be another device. Studio can show a phone-sized screen, but it is still your computer underneath.
terms.hardware: The real, physical device, like an actual phone or tablet.
terms.thermal throttling: When a device gets hot and slows itself down to cool off. A game might run at 60 FPS at first and drop to 40 after 10 minutes.
terms.memory pressure: When the device is running low on RAM because the game, the system, and other apps all need some.
terms.input latency: The delay between touching or pressing a button and the game reacting.
terms.RAM: A device's short-term memory. A phone with 3 GB of RAM has much less room than a PC with 16 GB.
terms.Passmark: A test that gives a device a speed score. Over half of Roblox players have devices scoring 10,000 to 20,000.
terms.cross-play: Players on phones, PCs, consoles, and tablets all playing together in the same game.
terms.jitter: When network delay keeps changing, like 50 ms, then 120 ms, then 60 ms. It makes movement look choppy.
terms.packet loss: When some bits of network data never arrive and have to be re-sent.
terms.touch target: The area of a button you can tap. Too small, and players miss it on a phone.
terms.pop-in: When objects suddenly appear as you get close, which can happen with streaming.

watchOut: Only testing on your own powerful computer. You are then testing for a small part of your players.
Testing for just a minute. Overheating and memory growth often only show up after 10 or more minutes.
Trusting desktop-sized buttons. Something easy to click with a mouse can be too small for a thumb on a 5-inch screen.
Using a Windows handheld as your only low-end test. These are great for checking controls but are much faster than a typical phone.
